question.text: Narmada Buyout Fund II (Category II AIF) is nearing its 7-year stated tenure with two portfolio companies still un-exited. The Manager proposes to extend the fund tenure by 2 years. What approval threshold and process applies?

answer.text: Approval of two-thirds of unit-holders by value of their investment; no SEBI approval required
Simple majority of unit-holders and prior SEBI approval
Unanimous consent of all investors and Trustees
Sponsor's unilateral discretion up to the extension cap

explanation.text: The Logic: Extension of tenure of close-ended Cat I/II AIFs is permitted up to 2 years, subject to approval of two-thirds of unit-holders by value of their investment in the AIF. If the required two-thirds consent is not obtained, the AIF must fully liquidate within 1 year following expiry of the tenure. The Trap: Option B wrongly imports a simple majority and a SEBI-approval requirement that the rule does not impose. Option C overstates the consent bar as unanimous. Option D wrongly grants the Sponsor unilateral discretion. Note: The workbook supports the two-thirds-by-value extension rule (up to 2 years) for close-ended Cat I/II AIFs and the one-year full-liquidation consequence if consent is not obtained.
